newsitem.title: UK: Berisford shares shine on bid approach.
newsitem.headline: Berisford shares shine on bid approach.

text.p: British consumer food equipment to agribusiness manufacturer Berisford Plc reported a dip in its annual pretax profits on Friday but its shares rode high after it said that it had received a possible takeover offer.
The shares surged 27-1/2 pence, or nearly 23 percent, to 148-1/2 pence in early trade on turnover of over one million shares.

Berisford said it had received "formal interest" in an offer being made for the company. It said the approach had "only been of a preliminary nature such that it is unclear whether it may or may not lead to an offer being made."
It gave no further details of the bid approach but said as a result it would postpone its plan to buy-back its convertible unsecured loan stock.
The company reported a slight dip in its pretax profit for the year ending September 28, 1996 to 25.5 million pounds ($42.93 million) from 26.8 million in the previous year.

But its turnover was higher at 497.5 million pounds up from 381.2 in the previous year. The company reported earnings per share of 12.5 pence and offered a total dividend of 4.5 pence per share, against last year's 3.0p.
It also said its sales and orders for the first seven weeks of the current financial year were higher compared to its performance in the previous year.
Berisford said its sales at Magnet were up 11 percent with retail kitchen orders 19 perecnt higher and kitchen sales despatched from its Darlington factory in north east England rose eight percent.
